newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - March 26.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - March 26.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Trading remained muted through Tuesday even as improving weather boosted consumption, Random Lengths said. Some buyers cited the Fed's announcement of a quarter-point rise in Fed funds as a reason not to buy. Many dealers also anticipate heavy offers of Canadian lumber with the new April 1 quota year.
But many secondaries and producers disagreed with the idea that Canadian shipments will pick up drastically in April.
Canadian fee-free lumber shipments as of March 18 were at 98 percent of annual quota for the year ending on March 31.

Western S-P-F trading was sloppy as mills contended with short order files and cautious buyers. Most customers looked for specific loadings that would fulfill immediate needs. Some producers focused on selling from reloads rather than chasing car business. The #2&Btr 2x6 was particularly vulnerable. A few mills cut 2x10 and 2x12 prices to compete with Hem-Fir, it said.
Eastern S-P-F prices drifted sideways in early-week trade.

Eastern S-P-F demand at the retail level improved but it provided little support as quota reallocations gave dealers additional buying opportunities. Many buyers remained on the fence. Many wholesalers, seeking discounts, bought sparingly.

Southern Pine producers reported a pickup in phone activity Tuesday although some calls were simply to check prices and availability. But mills booked enough business to keep prices on a firm-to-higher track. The #2 2x6 rose $2 central and westside.
Inland dimension mills had to work hard for orders. Most buyers stayed in fill-in posture and successfully countered mills, though desired tallies were not always available.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir sales improved Monday, though activity quieted for many mills on Tuesday. Demand for Douglas fir was not robust but supply thinned as mills switched to selling green stock. Hem-Fir prices were flat to lower.

Southern Pine plywood sheathing prices slumped, especially on the westside. Plentiful supplies at mills and ready availability from secondaries weighed heavily on the market. Some producers held quotes but opened up to counters.

Fir plywood sheathing and underlayment mills picked up orders at lower levels, giving some about a week of breathing room. A few mills firmed of raised quotes on certain items. One major sold out of 23/32-inch underlayment to early April, when its mill starts a 2-week shutdown for maintenance.

OSB sales were slow and mills fell back on order files built up during last week's rally. Most producers began the week at higher prices and held there, but most failed to sell much at the lower levels, Random Lengths said.
